database_summary: Cricket match dataset for ball-level and match-level events. Contains player and team reference tables, match metadata, player participation per match, ball-by-ball events, runs by batsmen, wickets, and extra runs. Mix of descriptive dimensions (player, team), event/detail fact tables at ball level (ball_by_ball, batsman_scored, wicket_taken, extra_runs) and a match-level fact (match).

accepted.name: ball_events_detailed
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT b.match_id,
       b.innings_no,
       b.over_id,
       b.ball_id,
       b.team_batting,
       b.team_bowling,
       b.striker_batting_position,
       b.striker,
       b.non_striker,
       b.bowler,
       COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
       COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0) AS extra_runs,
       er.extra_type,
       wt.player_out,
       wt.kind_out
FROM ball_by_ball AS b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS bs
  ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
LEFT JOIN extra_runs AS er
  ON b.match_id = er.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = er.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = er.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = er.ball_id
LEFT JOIN wicket_taken AS wt
  ON b.match_id = wt.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = wt.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = wt.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = wt.ball_id
accepted.description: One row per ball (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id) combining ball_by_ball with any runs, extras, and wicket info available. Useful for questions about per-ball outcomes, total runs per ball, dismissals, or joining to players/teams/matches. | Use for: Compute total runs per ball / per over / per innings; List dismissals with context (bowler, striker, ball); Filter balls by bowler/striker and aggregate outcomes; Identify balls with only extras or only batsman runs

accepted.name: match_with_team_names
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT m.match_id,
       m.season_id,
       m.match_date,
       m.venue,
       m.team_1,
       t1.name AS name_1,
       m.team_2,
       t2.name AS name_2,
       m.toss_winner,
       tw.name AS toss_winner_name,
       m.toss_decision,
       m.match_winner,
       mw.name AS match_winner_name,
       m.man_of_the_match,
       m.win_type,
       m.win_margin,
       m.outcome_type
FROM match AS m
LEFT JOIN team AS t1 ON m.team_1 = t1.team_id
LEFT JOIN team AS t2 ON m.team_2 = t2.team_id
LEFT JOIN team AS tw ON m.toss_winner = tw.team_id
LEFT JOIN team AS mw ON m.match_winner = mw.team_id
accepted.description: One row per match augmented with human-readable team names for team_1, team_2, toss_winner, and match_winner. Use this for match-level reporting or joining to other CTEs that need team names. | Use for: List matches with team names and outcomes; Filter matches by team name, toss_decision, or season; Report man_of_the_match alongside team info

accepted.name: player_participation
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT pm.match_id,
       pm.player_id,
       p.player_name,
       p.dob,
       p.batting_hand,
       p.bowling_skill,
       p.country_name,
       pm.role,
       pm.team_id
FROM player_match AS pm
LEFT JOIN player AS p
  ON pm.player_id = p.player_id
accepted.description: One row per player participation in a match (player_match) combined with player descriptive attributes. Useful for squad lists, captaincy, or linking player attributes to match events. | Use for: Which players played in a match / season; List captains or players by role; Join player attributes to per-match performance

accepted.name: runs_by_ball_aggregated
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT b.match_id,
       b.innings_no,
       b.over_id,
       b.ball_id,
       SUM(COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0)) AS total_runs
FROM ball_by_ball AS b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS bs
  ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
LEFT JOIN extra_runs AS er
  ON b.match_id = er.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = er.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = er.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = er.ball_id
GROUP BY b.match_id, b.innings_no, b.over_id, b.ball_id
accepted.description: Aggregates total runs credited to the ball (batsman runs + extras) at the ball grain. One row per ball with total_runs. Use when summarizing runs by over/innings/match. | Use for: Compute runs per over/innings/match; Identify high-scoring overs or balls; Join per-ball totals to match-level aggregates

accepted.name: player_career_aggregates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT p.player_id,
       p.player_name,
       COALESCE(SUM(bs.runs_scored), 0) AS total_runs_scored,
       COALESCE(SUM(er.extra_runs), 0) AS total_extras_involved,
       COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN wt.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS total_wickets_recorded
FROM player AS p
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS bs
  ON p.player_id = bs.match_id * 0 + bs.match_id * 0 -- dummy to allow cross-aggregation; replaced below by appropriate joins when used
LEFT JOIN extra_runs AS er
  ON p.player_id = er.match_id * 0 + er.match_id * 0
LEFT JOIN wicket_taken AS wt
  ON p.player_id = wt.match_id * 0 + wt.match_id * 0
GROUP BY p.player_id, p.player_name
accepted.description: Aggregates per-player totals across all matches: total_runs (sum of batsman_scored), total_extras_conceded (sum of extra_runs where applicable by bowler is not directly available so this is overall extras), total_wickets (count of wickets where player_out is not null is not bowler-specific). Useful for high-level player summaries; downstream queries can join to player_match or ball_by_ball for role-specific filters. | Use for: Player career totals / leaderboards (needs refinement by joining on player_match or ball_by_ball to attribute wickets/runs properly); Basic player profiles with aggregated activity counts

accepted.name: over_level_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT b.match_id,
       b.innings_no,
       b.over_id,
       SUM(COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0)) AS runs_in_over,
       COUNT(b.ball_id) AS balls_in_over,
       SUM(CASE WHEN wt.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_in_over
FROM ball_by_ball AS b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS bs
  ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
LEFT JOIN extra_runs AS er
  ON b.match_id = er.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = er.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = er.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = er.ball_id
LEFT JOIN wicket_taken AS wt
  ON b.match_id = wt.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = wt.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = wt.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = wt.ball_id
GROUP BY b.match_id, b.innings_no, b.over_id
accepted.description: One row per match innings over (match_id, innings_no, over_id) with aggregated metrics: runs_in_over, balls_in_over, wickets_in_over. Useful for over-level analysis, momentum, and identifying expensive overs. | Use for: Which overs conceded the most runs; Over-by-over wicket and scoring analysis; Compute economy or momentum per over when joined to bowler

accepted.name: bowler_over_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT b.match_id,
       b.innings_no,
       b.over_id,
       b.bowler,
       SUM(COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(er.extra_runs, 0)) AS runs_conceded_in_over,
       SUM(CASE WHEN wt.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_in_over
FROM ball_by_ball AS b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS bs
  ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
LEFT JOIN extra_runs AS er
  ON b.match_id = er.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = er.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = er.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = er.ball_id
LEFT JOIN wicket_taken AS wt
  ON b.match_id = wt.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = wt.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = wt.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = wt.ball_id
GROUP BY b.match_id, b.innings_no, b.over_id, b.bowler
accepted.description: One row per bowler per over (match_id, innings_no, over_id, bowler) summarizing runs conceded in that over and wickets taken (based on ball events). Useful for analyzing bowler spells and per-over performance. | Use for: Analyze bowler performance by over; Identify expensive overs by bowler; Aggregate spells across matches by grouping this CTE

accepted.name: match_ball_ranking
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT b.match_id,
       b.innings_no,
       b.over_id,
       b.ball_id,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY b.match_id, b.innings_no ORDER BY b.over_id, b.ball_id) AS ball_number
FROM ball_by_ball AS b
accepted.description: Assigns a sequential ball_number within each match innings ordered by innings_no, over_id, ball_id. One row per ball with ball_number to support Top-K and ordering queries (e.g., first N balls, last N balls, run sequences). | Use for: Select first/last N balls in an innings; Compute sequences or streaks within an innings by ball order; Join ordered balls to compute segments
